newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Interest Rate Increase.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Interest Rate Increase.

text.p: Following are a selection of analysts' comments following news that the Bank of England has raised official interest rates by a quarter percentage point.
DAVID COLEMAN, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT CIBC INVESTMENT BANK

"Mr Clarke has finally given to Mr George. He's finally been worn down by the Governor. It's not necessarily bad news. It's far enough away from election for electorate to forget about it. Damage will be limited.
"It's probably better to do it now and get the bad news out of the way than do it in March."
JEREMY PEAT, CHIEF ECONOMIST, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"The wieght of evidence indicated that, without some rapid monetary tightening, the Chancellor was in danger of both missing his inflation target and losing some hard won credibility. This move helps on both counts."
MARTIN BROOKES, ECONOMIST AT GOLDMAN SACHS

"It's not out of the ordinary for rates to go up this far away from the election. It would be more unsual if rates were to go up within the final three months before the election. Maybe the Chancellor thinks if he needs to raise rates it would be better to do it now as it will get increasingly difficult to raise rates clos to the election."

- "The Bank of England has got its way and the minimum lending rate has been set at six percent. The tightening has come well ahead of our expectations and must be good news for the credibility of the government's anti-inflation policy. To this end, the news should be a medium term positive for gilts and certainly supportive of sterling."
"The near term risk is that the market interprets today's move as a precursor to a loose budget." TIM FOX, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST AT STANDARD CHARTERED
"By moving now he (Clarke) is probably looking to head off any question of a much bigger move in interest rates just immediately ahead of the election."
